asm-sparse: No change to our sparse inner loop; park priority 3 (Zen 5 1T vs Swift) for this run. Why: compiled loops verified against the dump: one byte RMW per composite in all three entries, which is the floor under the base rules for p >= 113; ours equals Rust's instruction for instruction and beats Swift's (spill reloads). A 2x-unrolled variant screened no better (0.71 vs 0.67 cyc/bit). Any remaining sparse gain is in the memory system, which needs perf counters, not a code change. Passed over: cache-blocking the sparse primes (changes the outer loop shape; rules risk) and an AVX-512 scatter-OR (likely slow on Zen). Expect: next run: one perf-counter task (stores per cycle, L1D misses in the sparse phase) to tell the store limit from L2 waits.
